critiques.verdict: Yes, the lines now converge the way they do in the liked picture. I traced them by hand on the render. The measuring tool's answer of (0.683, 0.499) rests on only 13 lines, most of them the level eaves of houses that step up the 4-degree hill, so I didn't use it. The kerbs and gutters meet at 0.684 across, 0.440 down; in the liked picture they meet at 0.706, 0.424. The left roofline lies on the liked picture's yellow line (31.3 against 31.5 degrees). Both kerbs are within about 6 degrees: the left kerb enters the left edge at 0.57 instead of 0.60, and the right kerb leaves the bottom edge at 0.43 instead of 0.33. The pattern is the same: lines fan from the bottom left into the board's top-left corner. The rest of the geometry passes. The camera is level and on the pavement. The pit column (wheels 0.62, gate 0.60, drum 0.63) and the notice column (lamp 0.77, notice 0.84, chair 0.84) each line up. The main rule's four spots fit in a box 0.26 wide and 0.31 tall. The notice holds 67% of the brightest 3%. The top-left sky (0.04 to 0.42 across, 0.02 to 0.14 down, brightness 0.22) is clear and dim for the titles. What still separates our frame from the liked picture is the lighting and two prop placements, not the camera. First, the fire's light sits only 0.25 m above the coals, so the drum casts a shadow ring about 1.5 m wide. That ring is the hard black wedge over 32% of the bottom-left quarter. Outside it the road is floodlit and a bright band runs along the bottom edge. Warm light covers 11.2% of the frame (the liked picture: 2.3%), and its centre is at the drum's foot (0.55, 0.75) instead of by the notice (0.71, 0.55). Second, the notice, the board's frame, the chair and the drum's lit side are all close to white and merge into one shape. The liked picture has a cream notice on a dark board. Third, the chair faces the wrong way: its back is to the fire and the lantern is hidden behind it. Fourth, the notice's right edge is at 0.93, and rule 12 requires 0.90 or less. Fix these four before painting. The other faults are small. Do not move the camera again.

faults.fault: The drum's own fire light casts a long, hard-edged black shadow across the bottom-left road and floods everything outside it with warm light
faults.where: Dark wedge 0.00-0.52 across, 0.72-1.00 down: 8.5% of the frame, 32% of the bottom-left quarter, brightness 0.21. Its top edge is a flat bar at 0.75 down running from 0.33 to the kerb at 0.52; its slanted edge runs from (0.00, 0.97) to (0.33, 0.75). Around it the road is floodlit (0.00-0.50 across, 0.69-0.95 down, brightness 0.50). A bright band of pavement runs along the bottom edge (0.55-1.00 across, 0.96-1.00 down, brightness 0.74). In the street, the wedge covers the road from the kerb face out to x of about 1.6, between y 20.9 and 23.3.
faults.why_it_matters: Rule 8: the biggest dark shape in the frame sits where the eye enters, and its flat top edge reads as a bar across the road just below the drum. Rule 6: warm light covers 11.2% of the frame (target 1.5-3; liked picture 2.3). 40% of that warm light is in the bottom-left quarter, and its centre is at (0.55, 0.75), the drum's foot, not the notice (liked picture: 0.71, 0.55). The liked picture's bottom-left quarter is an even mid-tone (0.324, its own average), with only a short soft shadow at the drum's foot. Flux will keep this pattern of light and dark. In the painting with the props painted out it would leave a shadow and a fire glow with no drum. The cause: the drum's 900 W point light is only 0.25 m above the coals, about 0.24 m above the rim. The rim blocks it within about 1.3-1.7 m of the drum's axis (about 1.35 m on the pavement), and everything beyond that is lit. The bright band at the bottom edge is the outer edge of that ring.
faults.fix: Call brazier_fire(DRUM.x, DRUM.y, light_above_coals=0.7), which puts the light where the live flames will be. Then set the drum's light energy from 900 to about 300 W and its shadow softness (shadow_soft_size) from 0.25 to 0.4 m. The ring shrinks to about 0.7 m across, a soft curved shadow reaching about 0.4 m into the road. To keep the notice lit from below, add a second warm spot light 0.25 m above the coals, aimed at the notice's centre, cone about 40 degrees, about 150 W, so it does not reach the road. Targets for the re-render: warm light 1.5-3% of the frame with at least 60% of it in the right third; the bottom-left quarter within 0.03 of the frame's average brightness; no hard shadow edge more than 0.5 m from the drum. Make the props-free plate in Blender with the drum and its lights hidden, instead of painting them out.

faults.fault: The notice is almost pure white and does not stand apart from its board, the chair or the drum
faults.where: Notice paper (0.755-0.931 across, 0.508-0.644 down): brightness 0.96, 64% of its pixels pure white, and its top third (0.97) brighter than its bottom third (0.94), with no colour. Board's left post (0.70-0.73 across): 0.945, partly pure white. Board's top cap (0.68-1.00 across, 0.44-0.46 down): nearly white. Planks 0.54-0.62. Drum's lit right half (0.64-0.72 across, 0.66-0.78 down): 0.82. Chair seat: 0.69, 24% pure white.
faults.why_it_matters: Rules 5 and 6. In the squint view the notice, the board, the chair and the drum's right half merge into one white block (0.65-1.00 across, 0.43-0.80 down). The subject reads as a white board, not a notice on a board. The liked picture has a cream notice (0.61) on a dark board (0.38, 1.6 times darker) beside a dark drum (0.26), and the notice is warm at the bottom and cool at the top. Flux paints from these light and dark values, so it will paint a white smear and wash out the lettering. The bright cap is also a hard bar at the height where the lines meet.
faults.fix: After the first fix: turn the lantern's light down from 60 to about 15 W (its flicker is added live in the film). Darken the board's grey-timber material to about half its base colour so the posts, cap and planks come out at 0.30-0.40. Dirty the chair's white paint a little so its seat stays at 0.55 or below. Aim for the paper at 0.75-0.85, with nothing pure white, warmer at the bottom than at the top (the spot light from the first fix does this). Keep the drum's lit side at 0.5 or below. Then check that the notice is still at least 1.8 times the frame's average brightness (now 2.96) and holds at least 40% of the brightest 3% (now 67%).

faults.fault: The chair faces the wrong way: its back is to the fire and the lantern is hidden behind the back's slats
faults.where: Chair at 0.71-0.97 across, 0.62-0.84 down. Its back (uprights at 0.71-0.86 across) is the part nearest the camera and the drum. The seat runs away to the right, with the front legs at 0.955-0.97. The lantern (0.77-0.83 across, 0.65-0.75 down) stands behind the back's centre slat (the splat) and the other slats. The back's left upright runs along the drum's right edge at about 0.73 across, 0.64-0.83 down, 0-15 px apart.
faults.why_it_matters: Rule 9 and the liked picture call for the chair's back to the notice, its seat turned to the fire and a lit lantern on the seat, which says 'someone sat here by the fire and has just stepped away'. Ours reads as a chair turned away from the fire, facing the house wall. The lantern does not register as a light (none of the brightest 3%), though it is one of the story's lights in the liked picture. The upright lying along the drum's edge breaks rule 4. The script puts the lantern at CHAIR + (-0.10, -0.12) and calls that the front of the seat, but the back ended up there. The chair model evidently faces the opposite way from what CHAIR_TURN_DEGREES = 140 assumed.
faults.fix: Turn the chair 180 degrees: CHAIR_TURN_DEGREES from 140 to -40. Keep the lantern's offset, which then really is the front of the seat, facing the drum and the camera. On the re-render, check three things. The lantern's glass is clear in front of the chair's back, against the dark board. The chair's back either overlaps only the notice's bottom strip (the signature) by at least 14 px or clears it by at least 18 px. No upright is within 18 px of the drum's edge.

faults.fault: The notice reaches too far right, into the phone-button area (rule 12), and sits further from where the lines meet than in the liked picture
faults.where: The notice's right edge is at 0.931 across (liked picture: 0.914). The board's right side reaches 0.99, leaving a 10 px sliver of house wall at the frame edge. The chair's front leg (0.955-0.97) and the pail's right rim (0.958) line up under the board's right post. All of this is inside the area where video apps put their buttons (right edge, 0.45-0.90 down). The notice's top-left corner is 76 px right of and 131 px below where the lines meet; in the liked picture it is about 41 px right and 54 px below.
faults.why_it_matters: Rule 12: the notice must end at or left of 0.90, and unimportant edges at 0.95. Rule 4: edges should not just meet the frame edge or each other. The kit says to copy the sketch's composition, not this fault in it. The liked picture's lines meet on the board's left edge, just under its roof, close to the notice. Ours meet at the board's outer corner.
faults.fix: Move the board (with its posts), the chair, the lantern and the pail 0.12 m toward the road: board x from 3.40 to 3.28, chair from 3.34 to 3.22, pail from 3.36 to 3.24. Raise the board 0.15 m (BOARD_LIFT from 0.60 to 0.75). Keep the camera where it is, keep the drum at 2.81 against the kerb, and keep the lamp post at 3.25 (moved left, its glass would sit on the right winding wheel). Projected results: notice right edge about 0.89, board about 0.96, chair about 0.93, pail about 0.90. The notice's top-left corner would be 21 px right of and 72 px below where the lines meet. The lines would then meet on the board's left post, 45 px below its top, as in the liked picture. The drum's rim still covers the board's bottom-left corner (about 100 x 36 px) and stays about 46 px below the notice's bottom-left corner. Keep the live flames and smoke left of 0.70 across. Do not turn the camera instead: that would move where the lines meet to 0.65 across, further from the liked picture's 0.71.

faults.fault: Edges just touch at the spot where the lines meet: a far street lamp touches the board's post top, and the post tops stick up above the board
faults.where: Where the lines meet (0.684, 0.440). The far gas lamp gas_lamp_4 (in the street at 3.03, 64.5; in the frame at 0.68-0.695 across, 0.405-0.42 down) has its arm touching the top of the board's left post, and its post runs down the left end of the board's cap. The board's two posts stick up 0.12 m (about 45 px) above the cap as pale blocks at 0.70-0.73 and about 0.96 across.
faults.why_it_matters: Rule 4: two edges just touching, at the most looked-at point in the frame, make the far lamp look stuck to the board. After the move in the fault above, the lamp head would sit on the board's top edge instead, still touching.
faults.fix: Remove gas_lamp_4's post, glass and light, as the script already does for gas_lamp_2 (the liked picture has no lamp there). Cut the posts to the board's top: make their height BOARD_LIFT + 1.18 + 0.02 instead of BOARD_LIFT + 1.18 + 0.12.

faults.fault: The left half is a black, empty mass, so the frame's weight is lopsided
faults.where: The left houses (0.00-0.37 across, 0.26-0.47 down) average 0.14, darker than the sky (0.25); in the squint view they and the far road form one black mass. Only one work prop is in frame: the cart (0.03-0.19 across, 0.50-0.57 down). The sacks at (-3.5, 28.9) and the dustbins at (-3.6, 27.2) fall outside the left edge (they would appear at about -0.16 and -0.32 across), and the barrel at (3.72, 30.6) is behind the board.
faults.why_it_matters: Rule 10: the weight splits 34.5 to 65.5 per cent, left to right; it needs to be between 40 and 60 (the liked picture: 42.8 to 57.2). The quiet side should be dim but finely detailed: brick, windows, one or two small lights, small dark work props. The liked picture's left side has mid-tone brick, a lit wall lamp, lit windows, sacks and a cart. A black left half also leaves Flux to invent detail there or leave a hole.
faults.fix: Turn up the cool moonlight or sky light on the left house fronts until the brick reads about 0.22-0.28, no brighter than the sky. Light 2 or 3 more windows on the left row between 0.30 and 0.45 down. Move the coal sacks to (-3.4, 34.0), which lands at about 0.10 across, 0.54 down, behind the cart. Move the dustbins to (-3.4, 38.0), about 0.21 across, 0.52 down. Each should cover at most 2% of the frame and be darker than the frame's average. Then measure the split again.

faults.fault: The corner gas lamp's glass is plain white, not a warm gas glow
faults.where: Lamp glass at 0.715-0.83 across, 0.09-0.22 down: brightness 0.83 with no colour (it does not show on the warm-light map). It is the brightest thing outside the story group.
faults.why_it_matters: Rule 5: nothing large and bright in the top third, and the notice must win. Rule 6: in the liked picture this lamp is a warm amber glow (0.52) at the top of the notice's column. A white box will probably be painted as an electric light, which is wrong for gas in 1926, and it pulls the eye toward the sky where the titles go.
faults.fix: In assemble_notice_corner.py, change the glass glow from make_glow(m, (1.0, 0.72, 0.4), 2.5) to about colour (1.0, 0.6, 0.25) at strength 1.0, so the glass reads about 0.55, amber, and clearly darker than the notice.

faults.fault: The notice is smaller and squarer than in the liked picture, while the props in front of it are bigger
faults.where: Notice paper 190 x 262 px (0.176 across by 0.136 down; 2.4% of the frame), shaped about 1 to 1.4, with its top at 0.508 down.
faults.why_it_matters: In the liked picture the notice is the largest bright shape: 3.3% of the frame, a tall sheet shaped about 1 to 2 that reaches up to 0.45, just below where the lines meet. Ours is about a quarter smaller, while our drum (4.6% against 3.1%) and pail (2.7% against 1.8%) are about half as big again. The subject is outweighed by the props in front of it (rule 5, main rule).
faults.fix: Make the paper about 0.10 m taller at the top, about 0.53 x 0.80 m instead of about 0.53 x 0.70 m, keeping at least 0.1 m of plank above it. Together with the 0.15 m lift in the rule 12 fix, its top comes to about 0.46 down. Keep the drum, chair and pail at their current sizes (rule 8: the same sizes in every shot).

faults.fault: The kerbs still differ slightly from the liked picture's lines (this was the user's complaint)
faults.where: Kerbs and gutters meet at 0.684, 0.440 (liked picture: 0.706, 0.424). The left kerb enters the left edge at 0.57 (liked picture: 0.60), at 18.6 degrees against 24.0. The right kerb leaves the bottom edge at 0.43-0.45 (liked picture: 0.33), at 75.7 degrees against 69.7. The left roofline is at 31.3 degrees against 31.5. The houses' own level eaves meet 0.06 lower, at (0.684, 0.50), because each house steps up the 4-degree hill.
faults.why_it_matters: The complaint is answered: the same fan of lines runs from the bottom left into the board's top-left corner, the roofline lies on the liked picture's yellow line, and where the lines meet is within 0.022 across and 0.016 down. The remaining kerb difference comes from where our camera stands: 0.46 m from the kerb face with the eye 1.81 m up, where the liked picture's kerbs suggest about 0.70 m and 1.91 m. So its near kerb is a longer diagonal, while ours is a little more upright and shows the wide dark gutter at the bottom. The difference is small. The eaves' meeting point sits right beside the notice's top-left corner, so it helps.
faults.fix: Leave. A full match would need the camera moved from x 2.96 to 3.20 and the eye from 1.81 to 1.91 m, with the whole group moved 0.24 m toward the houses, which would leave the board 0.07 m from the house fronts. Turning the camera 0.8 degrees further left to reach 0.706 would push the notice to 0.95. Neither is worth it. The tool's (0.683, 0.499) is the eaves' meeting point, found from only 13 lines; go by the kerbs' 0.684, 0.440.

faults.fault: The story group is a little wide, and the drum stands right on the kerb's edge
faults.where: Story props span 0.52-0.97 across (0.456 wide). The drum's base is 0.015 m from the kerb face, so the kerb line runs into its bottom-left corner at about 0.52 across, 0.80-0.84 down (17 px gap).
faults.why_it_matters: Rule 3 checks for a box at most 0.40 wide, and rule 4 wants a gap of at least 18 px at this frame size. The liked picture has both of the same faults (0.464 wide; its drum also stands at the kerb's back edge). The rule 12 move narrows the group to about 0.42.
faults.fix: Leave. Moving the drum further onto the pavement would push it into the notice's lower-left corner after the rule 12 move.

critiques.verdict: Nothing in the frame is out of period for 1 May 1926. The notice wording is historically right: the government subsidy ended on Friday 30 April 1926, and the owners' notices closed the pits from Saturday 1 May unless the men accepted new terms. The gas lamp with its ladder bar, the setts and flagstones, the sash windows, the steel headframe, the brick chimney, the shut gates with the idle tub, and a few lit upstairs windows all fit a pit row at dusk. The story the user liked is broken by two faults, and both must be fixed before painting because the painting will keep whatever is in the plate. First, the chair is turned the wrong way. The chair model's back is on its +y side, so the script's 140 degrees points the back at the camera and the seat at the board and the house wall 0.5 m away. The lantern sits hidden behind the back's slats, so the frame now says "a chair seen from behind, facing the notice" instead of "someone sat here by the fire and has just stepped away". Second, the coals in the drum render as white stones on flat orange card. One cheap fix should go in before the painting as well. The drum's wall is 4 cm from the timber board and its paper notice, so the fire would scorch them, and its light bleaches the board planks (0.87) and the notice (0.975), which washes out the dates. Moving the board 0.5 m back and scaling it 1.11 about the camera's eye leaves the frame unchanged and solves this. It also puts the board right against the lamp post, which explains why a notice board stands on the pavement. The rest can stay as it is. The handcart reads empty, which is right for day one of the lockout. The lit windows are believable. The colliery chimney should smoke thinly at most.

faults.fault: The kitchen chair is turned 180 degrees from what the script intended. Its back faces the camera and the street, its seat faces the board and the house wall, and the lantern on the seat is hidden behind the back's slats.
faults.where: The chair spans 0.71-0.97 across and 0.62-0.84 down, with the back on the left near the drum and the seat running up-right. The lantern is at 0.77-0.83 across, 0.70-0.75 down, behind the slats.
faults.why_it_matters: In kitchen-chair.glb the back is on the model's +y side (the mean y of its top quarter is +0.245 m), so CHAIR_TURN_DEGREES = 140 points the back at 230 degrees (toward the camera and the drum) and the seat at 50 degrees, into the board 0.5 m away. A sitter would face the notice at knee distance with their back to the fire. Rule 9 ('back to the notice, seat turned to the fire, lantern lit on the seat') fails, and so does the sentence the user liked. Flux will paint exactly this.
faults.fix: Set CHAIR_TURN_DEGREES from 140 to -40, which is what the script's comment means, and keep CHAIR at (3.34, 21.75). The seat then faces 230 degrees, between the fire and the camera, and the back stands about 0.28 m in front of the board. Its top rail lands about 0.61 down, below NEW TERMS (bottom about 0.60) and over the signature. The existing lantern offset (-0.10, -0.12) then lands at the front of the seat, in view at about 0.80 across. Re-render and check three things: (a) the back's right edge is at or left of 0.95 across, and if not use -30; (b) the chair's front-right leg is at least 0.1 m from the drum's wall (it is about 0.07 m at -40 and 0.13 m at -30); (c) the lantern's top clears the notice's bottom edge (predicted only about 9 px apart; if they just touch, set LANTERN_SCALE from 1.4 to 1.25), and its globe reads lit and warm.

faults.fault: The fire's coals render as white stones on flat orange card.
faults.where: The top of the drum, 0.54-0.70 across, 0.63-0.65 down (mean brightness 0.75, peaks 1.0).
faults.why_it_matters: brazier_fire heaps the coals flush with the rim (top = ground + 0.80 on a 0.856 m drum) and puts a 900 W light 0.25 m above them. Even the dark lumps (only 1 in 4) light up near white. The painter will paint white rocks or ice in the drum, and the film's live flames will rise out of them. A lockout fire burned coal or picked coal, cinders and wood: dark lumps with an orange glow between them.
faults.fix: In brazier_fire: set top = ground + 0.70 (coal bed 0.15 m below the rim). Pass light_above_coals = 0.35 so the light stays at its current height of about 1.05 m. Make 3 lumps in 4 dark instead of 1 in 4, raise the dark roughness from 0.5 to 0.9, and raise the glowing emission strength from 1 to about 6-8. Check a crop of the drum top: it should read as dark coal with orange gaps (mean about 0.35-0.5), with no white faces.

faults.fault: The fire stands against the notice board: the drum's wall is about 4 cm from the board's lower-left corner and left post. The freestanding board also blocks 0.72 m of a 1.47 m pavement, 0.75 m in front of a lamp post.
faults.where: Where the drum overlaps the board's lower-left corner (0.69-0.75 across, 0.63-0.68 down). The bleached board planks are at 0.70-0.75 across, 0.48-0.65 down. The notice is at 0.75-0.93 across, 0.51-0.645 down.
faults.why_it_matters: Nobody lights a brazier 4 cm from a timber board with a paper notice on it; the corner would scorch. The closeness is visible in the frame: the fire's light bleaches the planks (0.87, nearly as bright as the notice at 0.975) and washes out the notice's two date lines, which anchor the story. During the 1.5 m slide the parallax shows the drum and the board stuck together. Colliery notices went on the pit gate, the colliery office, or a board fixed to a wall or lamp post, not on a freestanding board in mid-terrace.
faults.fix: Move the board back without changing the frame by scaling it about the camera's eye. Set BOARD from (3.40, 22.25) to (3.45, 22.75), BOARD_SCALE from 1.0 to 1.11 and BOARD_LIFT from 0.60 to 0.46. The board and notice land on the same pixels and the slide's direction is unchanged (the notice centre stays on the same line). The drum's wall is then about 0.45-0.5 m clear of the timber, the fire's light on the board drops to roughly a quarter, and the board stands about 0.2 m in front of the lamp post at (3.25, 23.0), so it reads, and is, fixed to the post. If the lamp's base meets the board's left post, move LAMP_POST to y 23.05. Afterwards check that the notice paper sits at about 0.8-0.9 brightness with the dates legible. If it is still above 0.95, lower brazier_light from 900 W to about 500 W.

faults.fault: The chair is clean bright white, the second-brightest thing in the frame.
faults.where: The chair seat (0.76-0.95 across, 0.72-0.75 down) at brightness 0.70; the back's top rail (0.72-0.83 across, 0.625-0.64 down) at 0.77.
faults.why_it_matters: A pristine white chair reads as modern. In a 1926 pit cottage, kitchen chairs were scrubbed deal, dark-stained, or painted and grimy. Its brightness also competes with the notice (rule 5).
faults.fix: Multiply the chair's base colour by about 0.6 and warm it to a dirty cream, about (0.55, 0.50, 0.42), with worn paint on the seat front and the top rail. Aim for the seat at about 0.45-0.5 brightness in the render, well below the notice.

faults.fault: The handcart is a coal merchant's cart and its coal sacks carry a merchant's stencils, but in this frame the sacks are hidden in the cart's box and the cart reads empty. The sacks against the left houses are out of frame.
faults.where: The handcart at 0.03-0.19 across, 0.50-0.57 down. The wall sacks at (-3.5, 28.9) project to about -0.17 across, off the left edge, and are also off the start frame.
faults.why_it_matters: An empty handcart is the better reading for the evening of 1 May. Loose concessionary coal stopped with the lockout, merchants had nothing to sell to men without wages, and coal picked from the tips in sacks and handcarts is a story of the weeks that followed. Full merchant's sacks would say coal is plentiful.
faults.fix: Leave the cart as it is. In the painting prompt, call it 'an empty handcart' so Flux does not invent full sacks. If the sacks inside the cart could show once painted, delete them, since they do nothing for this frame.

faults.fault: The camera eye is 1.81 m above the pavement under it, the eye height of a man about 1.93 m tall. Men in 1926 averaged about 1.68 m (eye height about 1.57 m).
faults.where: The whole frame (the camera at x 2.96, y 17.85).
faults.why_it_matters: Rule 2 asks for standing eye height. Because the street rises 4 degrees, the eye is only about 1.52 m above the ground where the drum and chair stand (my measurement of the drum's rim and base agrees), so the story group is seen as a 1.6-1.65 m person would see it. Changing the height would move the props in the frame the user approved.
faults.fix: No change.

faults.fault: The lamp post stands mid-pavement, 0.75 m in from the kerb face; period posts stood at the kerb edge, about 0.3-0.45 m in.
faults.where: The lamp head at 0.72-0.83 across, 0.09-0.21 down; the shaft at 0.77 across down to the top of the board at 0.445.
faults.why_it_matters: It is a slight oddity, but moving the post 0.3 m toward the kerb would put it about 0.68 across, right over where the lines meet and the colliery gate. From this camera it rises out of the board and reads as the post the board is fixed to, which is plausible (and becomes literal with the board fix above).
faults.fix: No change.

faults.fault: The lit windows are lit upstairs, with the ground-floor front rooms dark.
faults.where: The left terrace at 0.21-0.33 across, 0.31-0.39 down (mean 0.31-0.48, warm colour about (0.6, 0.46, 0.33)).
faults.why_it_matters: This is believable. In a two-up-two-down the front downstairs room was the parlour kept for best and the family lived in the back kitchen, so lit front bedrooms at dusk (children going to bed) and dark parlours fit. The amber colour suits gas or paraffin light, and the windows stay well below the notice's brightness.
faults.fix: Keep it to these 3 or 4 windows, amber and dim. Do not add lit windows near the notice.

faults.fault: The colliery chimney, headframe and gates (a smoke note for the live layer and the painting prompt).
faults.where: The chimney at 0.45-0.50 across, 0.08-0.50 down; the winding wheels at 0.52-0.72 across, 0.20-0.25 down.
faults.why_it_matters: All of it is right for 1926: a boiler chimney, a steel headframe, still wheels, shut gates and an idle tub. During the lockout the boilers kept going only for pumping and ventilation, so the liked picture's heavy plume would say the pit is working. Domestic ranges were still lit on day one, so a few thin wisps from house chimneys are true; none at all would look weeks into the lockout.
faults.fix: If smoke is drawn live or named in the painting prompt, use a thin wisp from the colliery chimney and a few faint wisps from house chimneys.

faults.fault: The full-height rolled-hoop oil-drum brazier and the coopered wooden pail are slightly off-typical for 1926.
faults.where: The drum at 0.52-0.73 across, 0.63-0.83 down; the pail at 0.80-0.96 across, 0.82-0.93 down.
faults.why_it_matters: The oil-drum brazier is the iconic image of the 1984-85 strike pickets; in 1926 an iron 'fire devil' (a perforated bucket on legs) was more usual, and by then a galvanised bucket was more common than a wooden pail. Still, steel drums existed in 1926, the punched air holes make it a real brazier, and the user liked both props.
faults.fix: No change. Optionally, 4-6 small coal lumps in the bottom of the pail would say 'they fed the fire from this'.

critiques.verdict: The slide works geometrically only if the right picture gets painted. assemble_notice_corner.py and notice-corner.js draw the plate from the start of the slide (1536 x 2730, 64.4 degree lens), and the whole composed frame lies inside that plate, so nothing at the edges runs off the painting. The brief, though, says "this frame will be repainted". If composed-end.png itself were painted, 29% of the first frame would have no painting. I rebuilt the scene with the brief's positions (they match facts-end within 1 cm) and cast rays from the start and end cameras. In the held end frame, 2.1% of the picture is surface the plate never saw and the planned paint-out does not cover. About 0.4% of that is the house front, rainwater pipe and trim behind the gas-lamp post, which NEAR_PROPS in notice-corner.js leaves out. Most of the rest are 1 to 4 px slivers beside drainpipes, eaves and the headframe lattice, and those can stay. Another 0.4% is prop surfaces uncovered from behind other props: the insides of the pail and drum, and the chair legs behind the pail. The bigger risk is the behind painting. In a band about 0.05 of the plate's height round every near prop, the background changes over to it during roughly the first fifth of the slide. That band is 12 to 17% of the frame, or 20 to 27% once the lamp post is added. So the behind painting must be the main painting with only the props repainted, not a new repaint. Several faults are baked into the painting and should be fixed in 3D before the paid repaint. The chair faces the wrong way: its back is to the fire and camera, and the lantern is seen through 9 px spindles. The lamp post's arm crosses the pithead, its head sits 22 to 26 px from the right wheel for the whole slide, and its glass is flat white at 0.91. The fire light sits only 0.2 m above the rim, so the drum shades a hard-edged dark patch 1.3 to 1.7 m out into the bottom left, and at 900 W it lights the near pavement to 0.56 in the first frame. The board's left post is 0.95, almost as bright as the notice at 0.97, and the film shows our own board texture, not the painter's. The lantern's top stays within 4 to 6 px of the notice's bottom edge from the first frame to the last. The newest script fixes the chair and the coals but still has the fire light at 1.05 m above the ground, the lamp post at turn 0 with its glass at 2.5, and the lamp post missing from NEAR_PROPS. Evidence is in <session folder> cat-A-overlay.png and cat-B-overlay.png show the uncovered areas (red: bare 3D texture; orange: prop surfaces uncovered; green: behind painting), the numbers are in analysis.json and analysis2.json, and start-film.png is a render of the first frame.

faults.fault: The brief says composed-end.png will be repainted, but the film shines the painting from the start of the slide (notice-corner-camera.json = start, 64.4 degree lens). If the end frame (60.4 degrees, from the end position) were painted instead, the first frame would have no painting in 29% of the picture.
faults.where: Start frame: bottom 16% (from 0.84 down to 1.0), a left strip 0.05 to 0.18 wide (widening downward from 0.14 down), a right strip 0.03 wide.
faults.why_it_matters: The opening seconds would show bare, darkened 3D textures at three edges. A plate cannot be drawn from the end position to cover this either: the pavement at the bottom of the first frame is about 1.7 m in front of the end camera and would need a lens of about 95 degrees.
faults.fix: Send Flux only the plate made by assemble_notice_corner.py --plate (start position 2.811, 16.357, 3.188; 1536 x 2730; 64.4 degrees). Use composed-end.png only as the composition check. Name the file notice-corner-painted.jpg so it pairs with notice-corner-camera.json.

faults.fault: The behind painting is planned as the same picture with the near props painted out by Flux. The film changes over to it in a band of about 0.05 of the plate's height (about 140 end-frame px) round the drum, chair, lantern, pail and board as soon as the camera has moved about 0.4 degrees around a point (quickMove), which is the first fifth or so of the slide.
faults.where: A ring covering 12 to 17% of the frame, inside 0.39 to 1.0 across and 0.34 to 1.0 down. Adding the lamp post makes it 20 to 27%.
faults.why_it_matters: A full Flux edit shifts colour, brushwork and light everywhere: the dark patch round the drum, the firelight on the road and kerb, the lamp's light on the house front. Any difference shows as a ring cross-fading round the story group just as the move starts.
faults.fix: Ask the painter for a masked paint-out only. The mask is the near props' outlines from the plate camera (an object-ID render), grown by about 12 plate px. Paste the main painting back over everything outside the mask, so the ring is identical pixel for pixel. As a guide for what continues behind the props, render a second 3D plate with the near props hidden from the camera but still casting shadows (Object > Visibility: Camera off, Shadow on; lights kept). Behind the drum: the kerb top and gutter running on to the board, the road setts, and the drum's dark patch. Behind the chair and pail: the pavement slab joints. Under the board's 0.6 m gap: the pavement, the house's base course and the lamp post's foot. Behind the board: the right terrace's wall, its window trim and its vertical rainwater pipe. Without the props, the start plate's right part (x > 0.6) shows pavement 40%, house wall 15%, trim 8%, rainwater pipes 8%, sky 11%.

faults.fault: The gas-lamp post is not in NEAR_PROPS in notice-corner.js, so the behind painting keeps it. Its 0.70 m ladder arm is a thin horizontal bar crossing the pithead lattice. During the slide the head rises 132 px and the arm 90 px over the house front, lattice and sky.
faults.where: Shaft 0.76 to 0.78 across, 0.42 to 0.73 down; head from 0.26 (start) to 0.19 (end) down, 0.72 to 0.83 across; arm from 0.34 to 0.29 down, 0.66 to 0.88 across. The uncovered house front, rainwater pipe and trim cover about 0.4% of the end frame, in a strip about 12 px wide right of the shaft from 0.20 to 0.47 down and a patch at 0.74 to 0.83 across, 0.22 to 0.30 down.
faults.why_it_matters: Those areas show bare, tinted 3D wall, or the painter's lamp post left behind as a ghost on the wall and lattice. The arm is about 8 px thick, so Flux will merge it with the lattice, and its painted copy stays on the pithead while the 3D arm moves.
faults.fix: Add 'gas-lamp-post' to NEAR_PROPS (it is 6.7 m from the plate camera, inside NEAR = 12) and include it in the paint-out mask. Before painting, turn the post 90 degrees (turn_degrees=90 in place_prop) so the arm points along the street and hides inside the shaft's outline. The head stays 22 to 26 px from the right winding wheel through the whole slide. The newest position (3.50, 23.25) should clear it, but check the gap is at least 25 px in both the first and the last frame.

faults.fault: The lamp's glass panes render flat white (0.91 luminance, 0.33% of the frame) in the top third, second only to the notice.
faults.where: 0.74 to 0.82 across, 0.15 to 0.20 down (end); 0.22 to 0.26 down at the start, where it is 0.86.
faults.why_it_matters: Flux will paint it as a glowing white block, possibly brighter than the notice. The film blooms anything over 0.9 (glowThreshold 0.9), so a blooming patch would slide 132 px up the top-right corner, competing with the notice and the titles.
faults.fix: For the gas lamp's glass, change make_glow(m, (1.0, 0.72, 0.4), 2.5) to about (1.0, 0.6, 0.3) at strength 0.8, so the panes read warm amber at about 0.6 to 0.7. Keep the 25-strength mantle as the small bright point.

faults.fault: The fire light is only 0.2 m above the drum's rim (z 2.73, 1.06 m above the ground; the newest script's 0.70 + 0.35 still gives 1.05 m). The rim therefore shades the ground out to 1.3 to 1.7 m from the drum, which makes the hard-edged dark wedge (0.22 luminance against 0.55 for the lit road beside it). At 900 W the fire also lights the near pavement to 0.56 in the first frame (frame average 0.31) and brings the warm share to 11% (target 1.5 to 3%).
faults.where: End frame: wedge 0.0 to 0.52 across, 0.73 to 1.0 down, where the eye enters. Start frame: bright empty pavement 0.62 to 1.0 across, 0.80 to 1.0 down.
faults.why_it_matters: It is big and dark in the bottom left (against rule 8), and its straight edges will be painted as a slab. The edge of the dark patch near the drum falls inside the behind-painting band and the live contact shadow is only 1.0 m across, so any mismatch shows round the drum's foot as the move starts.
faults.fix: Raise the fire light to about 0.45 m above the rim (z about 2.98, about 1.3 m above the pavement; in the newest script set FIRE_LIGHT_ABOVE_COALS to about 0.60 with COAL_TOP 0.70). Measured shaded distance: 0.77 to 0.92 m, against 1.3 to 1.7 m now (0.35 m above the rim gives 0.9 to 1.1 m). In brazier_fire set shadow_soft_size 0.25 to 0.35, turn on the light's soft-shadow jitter (use_shadow_jitter) for the plate render, and cut the energy from 900 W to about 300 W. Render the plate with at least 96 samples: at 16 samples the shadow edge is speckled, and Flux will paint speckle as gravel.

faults.fault: The kitchen chair is turned backwards in this frame (turn 140 degrees): its back faces the fire and the camera, and the lantern stands on the seat behind the back. The back's spindles are 9 px wide and the stretchers 6 px (about 8 and 6 px in the plate).
faults.where: Chair 0.70 to 0.97 across, 0.62 to 0.84 down; lantern 0.77 to 0.83 across, 0.65 to 0.75 down, seen through the spindles.
faults.why_it_matters: Flux will smear the spindles and the lantern into one shape. The live lantern glow sits behind the spindles. The empty chair no longer faces the fire, which weakens the story.
faults.fix: Use CHAIR_TURN_DEGREES = -40, as in the newest script (back to the board, seat to the fire), with the lantern on the front of the seat, clear of the spindles. Then check the lantern against the spindles and the notice in both the first and the last frame.

faults.fault: The lantern's top touches the notice's bottom edge for the whole slide: a 4 px overlap in the first frame, a 6 px gap in the last. They are at similar distances, so they move only about 10 px relative to each other.
faults.where: Around 0.79 to 0.83 across; 0.607 against 0.609 down at the start, 0.650 against 0.647 at the end.
faults.why_it_matters: This is the rule-4 just-touching edge on the subject, and no frame of the slide escapes it, because the props keep that relation throughout.
faults.fix: After the chair fix, set a gap of at least 25 px in the first frame by lowering the lantern about 0.08 m relative to the notice (for example, raise BOARD_LIFT by 0.08 m). Alternatively, set an overlap of at least 20 px in the last frame by lowering the notice about 0.06 m, covering only the signature, never NEW TERMS. Measure both ends.

faults.fault: The board's timber is pale and fire-lit: the left post is 0.95, the top rail 0.74 and the planks 0.6 to 0.8, against 0.97 for the notice. In the squint view the board and chair form one light block. notice-corner.js makes every board material an own surface (tinted like the notice paper), so the film shows our 3D timber, not the painter's.
faults.where: Board 0.68 to 1.0 across, 0.44 to 0.80 down; left post 0.70 to 0.72 across.
faults.why_it_matters: The notice does not stand out from its frame, and the painter cannot fix this, because the board's painted pixels are never shown. The board also reads as a 3D render inside a painting over about 4% of the frame, right at the subject.
faults.fix: Darken the board's grey-timber and black-boards in 3D (multiply the base colour by about 0.4, as tint() does for the chair) so the fire-lit post stays under about 0.45. If cheap, keep only 'notice-paper' as an own surface and let the timber wear the painting. In that case render the plate with a blank cream notice, so no garbled lettering spills onto the board, chair top or lantern.

faults.fault: The board's right side ends on the frame edge in the held frame, and the slide pushes it out over the last part of the move: right post from 0.952 to 0.991, panel from 0.965 to 1.0. The pail reaches 0.959 and the chair 0.974.
faults.where: 0.95 to 1.0 across, 0.42 to 0.80 down, where the phone apps' buttons sit.

faults.fix: Either crop it decisively (the post's right edge at 1.0 or beyond with at least 40 px off-frame, about 0.10 m further right) or bring it in to 0.95 or less (about 0.14 m left, or board scale about 0.85). Moving it left puts the board's left edge over the point where the street's lines meet (rule 1), so re-run the checker on the newest layout (board at 3.45, 22.75, scale 1.11) before choosing.

faults.where: 0.81 to 0.92 across, 0.77 to 0.82 down (end); about 0.82 to 0.91 across, 0.69 to 0.72 down at the start.

faults.fault: The tops of the near props are seen more from above at the end than in the plate: chair seat 11 to 15 degrees, pail rim 12 to 17, coal bed 7 to 10, which is 1.34 to 1.45 times more face-on. That is inside the film's frontStretch fade (1.3 to 1.9), so in the held frame they partly fade to their own 3D textures. The pail's inner wall (0.12% of the frame) and the drum's far inner wall and coals (0.07%) are uncovered for the first time.
faults.where: Seat 0.75 to 0.95 across, 0.73 to 0.76 down; pail rim 0.80 to 0.96 across, 0.77 to 0.82 down; coal bed 0.53 to 0.70 across, 0.63 to 0.65 down.

merged.convergence_note: Confirmed three ways: the hand-traced kerbs and gutters, the shot checker (0.684, 0.439), and the camera itself. A 6.87-degree left turn puts the point where the lines meet at 0.686 across, and the street's 4-degree rise puts it at 0.439 down. So the kerbs and gutters meet at about 0.684 across, 0.440 down. The liked picture's lines meet at 0.706, 0.424, which is 0.022 across and 0.016 down away. The fan of lines runs from the bottom left into the board's top-left corner, as in the liked picture. The measuring tool's (0.683, 0.499) is only the level eaves, which sit on the horizon at exactly 0.500 because the camera is level. The tool's (0.952, 0.617) on the newest render, from 9 lines, is noise. Do not turn the camera or change its height or lens. A sideways move without a turn (fix 2) leaves this point exactly where it is.
fix_in_3d_now: 1. ONE LIGHTING FIX for six faults the critics listed separately: the white notice, the pale board, the white chair seat, the white drum top, the warm light spilling too wide, and the warm light centred on the drum's foot. Measured on composed-end.png, then on the newest render, composed-end-2.png: notice 0.96 then 0.96 (85% pure white); board's left post 0.91 then 0.88; planks 0.81 then 0.65; chair seat 0.64 then 0.80 (54% pure white, worse, because the 60 W lantern sits on it with no shadow); drum top 0.75 then 0.975 (a white disc, 86% pure white); warm light 11.2% then 7.6% of the frame (target 1.5 to 3). Changes in set_dressing.py / assemble_notice_corner.py: (a) the drum's light from 900 to 300 W and shadow_soft_size from 0.25 to 0.35; (b) raise that light to about 0.40 m above the rim: FIRE_LIGHT_ABOVE_COALS from 0.35 to 0.55 with COAL_TOP 0.70, which puts it 1.25 m above the drum's ground; (c) the lantern's light from 60 to 15 W (its glass glow and the live flicker stay); (d) multiply the base colour of the board's 'grey-timber' and 'black-boards' by about 0.5. The film shows these as the board's own surfaces, not painted ones, so only a change in 3D reaches the film. Targets on a re-render: notice 0.75-0.85 with no more than 5% pure white; posts, cap and planks 0.30-0.40 (liked picture 0.30); chair seat 0.50 or less (liked 0.47); drum top 0.40-0.55 and orange, nothing pure white (liked 0.44); drum's lit side 0.5 or less; warm light 3% or less, mostly round the story props; the notice still at least 1.8 times the frame's average and holding at least 40% of the brightest 3%. If the notice is not warmer at its bottom than its top, add a warm spot light about 0.95 m above the drum's ground, aimed at the notice's centre, 40-degree cone, about 150 W. In notice-corner.js the live fireLight sits at coals + 0.12 m; move it to the Blender light's height so the board's own surface is lit the way the painting is.

2. KEEP THE NOTICE OUT OF THE PHONE-BUTTON STRIP (rule 12), which is confirmed: the notice's right edge is at 0.931, the board's right post at about 0.99 (14 px of wall beyond it), and the cap runs off the frame edge. Recommended fix: move the camera's end point 0.12 m sideways only: CAMERA_END x from 2.96 to 3.08, with the same height (1.81 m), the same 6.87-degree turn and the same lens. Where the lines meet stays at 0.684, 0.440, and the colliery, wheels and chimney move 3 px or less. Every near prop slides left together (board 41 px, drum 48, chair 50, pail 60), so their overlaps stay as composed-end-2 has them, within about 10 px. Predicted: notice right edge about 0.89, board's right post about 0.95, cap corner about 0.97 at 0.44 down (above the button strip), chair about 0.88, pail about 0.85, corner lamp head 38 px clear of the right winding wheel. It also brings the right kerb halfway to the liked picture: its angle goes from about 76 to about 73.5 degrees (liked 69.7) and it leaves the bottom edge at about 0.39 instead of 0.45 (liked 0.33). The camera is then 0.58 m in from the kerb face. If the camera must not move, the board-only alternative is BOARD x from 3.45 to 3.33. That alone lines up the notice's left edge with the drum's right edge (both at about 0.717), so also set DRUM x from 2.76 to 2.82, BOARD_LIFT from 0.46 to 0.54 and CHAIR x from 3.27 to 3.31. Do not raise the board 0.15 m: with the turned chair, that sets the notice's bottom edge right on the chair's top rail. After either fix, check three pairs of edges at 1080 wide (at least 18 px apart or at least 14 px overlapping). First, the board's left post against the pale stone strip on the right of the colliery doorway (0.648-0.656 across, 0.38-0.47 down): any shift of 33 to 103 px puts the post or the cap's end within a few px of it, so darken that strip to the brick colour in build_street.py. Second, the drum's right edge against the board's left post: only 9 px apart now (about 0.72 across), and 16 px after the camera move; move the posts in from dx ±0.36 to ±0.32 so at least 18 px of post shows. Third, the notice's bottom edge against the chair's top rail (now a 63 px overlap that covers only the signature, clear of NEW TERMS).

3. RENDER AND SEND THE RIGHT PICTURE. composed-end.png's hard black shape at bottom left (0.00-0.52 across, 0.72-1.00 down) is a render fault, not a lighting result. plate.log, which wrote composed-end.png, has 43 'Shadow buffer full ... (3126 / 2048)' errors. The shape's straight edges sit at x about 1.6-1.7 and y about 20.9 and 23.2, which is plus or minus 1.1-1.2 m from the foot of the fire's light, its height above the road. Those are the edges of the light's downward shadow-map face. composed-end-2.png has its light at the same 1.05 m and no errors in plate2.log, and shows only a soft gradient there. Before paying: render the plate with assemble_notice_corner.py --plate (start of the slide at 2.81, 16.36 or the new start if fix 2 moves the end, 1536 x 2730, 64.4-degree lens), because the film shines the painting from notice-corner-camera.json, which is the start. Use at least 64 samples, or 96 if the drum's soft shadow looks speckled, as it does at 16 in the slide critic's start-film.png. Reject any render whose log contains 'Shadow buffer full'; the larger plate needs more shadow memory, so raise shadow_pool_size above '1024' if needed. Use composed-end.png only to check the composition.

4. REMOVE gas_lamp_4 (post, glass and light, at 3.03, 64.5; on screen 0.68-0.695 across, 0.405-0.42 down), in the same loop that already removes gas_lamp_2. Its head is 5-7 px from the top of the board's left post in both renders, and it stands exactly where the lines meet. After fix 2 it would also stick up just above the cap. Cut the posts to the board's top: in wooden_post(...) the height becomes BOARD_LIFT + 1.18 * BOARD_SCALE + 0.02 instead of + 0.12. That removes the two pale blocks 45 px tall at 0.70-0.73 and about 0.96 across.

5. CORNER GAS LAMP GLASS: change '_glass' from make_glow(m, (1.0, 0.72, 0.4), 2.5) to about make_glow(m, (1.0, 0.6, 0.25), 1.0). Keep the bulb at 25 as the small bright mantle. Its glass now measures 0.81-0.84 and is nearly colourless, in the top third where the titles go; the film blooms anything above 0.9. Target 0.5-0.6 and amber (liked picture 0.49), clearly darker than the notice.

6. FILM CODE THAT DECIDES THE PAINT-OUT MASK: add 'gas-lamp-post' to NEAR_PROPS in notice-corner.js (confirmed missing; it stands 6.9 m from the plate camera, inside NEAR = 12). Include the post, its head and the sweep of its ladder arm in the behind painting's mask. Otherwise the wall uncovered beside the post as the camera slides shows a painted ghost post.

7. LEFT SIDE (rule 10), after fix 1, because dimming the right side moves the weight split by itself: re-measure the split (34.5/65.5 in composed-end, 31.6/68.4 in composed-end-2; the camera move in fix 2 also moves weight left). If the left side still has less than 40%, lift the left house fronts from 0.13 to about 0.17-0.19 with a cool fill light. That is about 0.65 of the sky's 0.27, the same ratio as the liked picture (0.25 against 0.40). Move the wall sacks from (-3.5, 28.9), which is outside the frame, to (-3.4, 34.0), about 0.10 across and 0.54 down. Move the dustbins to (-3.4, 38.0), about 0.21 across and 0.52 down. Add at most 1-2 more lit windows, dim and amber, 0.30-0.45 down.

8. PAIL HANDLE: delete the object wooden_bucket_01_handle, or lay it flat along the rim. It is a wire 5-7 px wide crossing the chair's front leg and the edge of its seat (0.81-0.92 across, 0.77-0.82 down). The painter will drop it or move it, and a painted copy left on the chair stays behind as a ghost while the 3D handle moves about 100 px during the slide.
ask_the_painter: Paint the plate made at the start of the slide (1536 x 2730), not composed-end.png. Keep every edge exactly where it is (use structure control or a low enough strength). The painting is shone back onto the same 3D shapes, so any edge that moves shows as a double outline when the camera slides. Check by laying the plate's edges over the painting.

Paint no flames, sparks or smoke (none from the drum, the colliery chimney or the house chimneys), and no people. These are drawn live in the film. The drum shows only a dim orange glow inside its top.
The corner street lamp is a gas lamp of 1926: a warm amber glass with a small bright mantle, not a white electric light. The lantern on the chair is a small warm paraffin glow.

The notice is a cream sheet, a little warmer at its bottom (lit from the fire and lantern below) than at its top. Do not invent or sharpen lettering on it or anywhere else; our own notice and board are laid over it in the film. The board is dark weathered timber. The chair is grubby cream, clearly darker than the notice.
Keep the top-left sky (0.04-0.42 across, 0.02-0.14 down) plain and dim for the titles: no bright clouds, moon or smoke plume there. The notice stays the brightest thing in the picture.

Second painting (props removed): paint out only inside a mask of the near props (drum, chair, lantern, pail, the board with its notice and posts, the corner lamp post), taken from an object-ID render of the plate camera and grown by about 12 plate px. Paste the main painting back, pixel for pixel, everywhere outside the mask. As a guide to what lies behind the props, use a 3D plate with those props hidden from the camera only (Object > Visibility: Camera off, shadows still on, all lights unchanged).
